question.prompt: A bakery owner turns on his doughnut machine at \(8{:}30\) am. At \(11{:}10\) am the machine has completed one third of the day’s job. At what time will the doughnut machine complete the job?

solutions.explanation:
Assume the machine maintains a constant production rate throughout the job. Then equal thirds of the job take equal amounts of time. From \(8{:}30\) am to \(11{:}10\) am is \(2\) hours \(40\) minutes, or \(160\) minutes. Since this completes one third, the whole job takes
\[
160\div\frac13=480\text{ minutes}=8\text{ hours}.
\]
Eight hours after \(8{:}30\) am is \(4{:}30\) pm.

The constant-rate assumption is necessary. For example, if the machine doubles its rate after \(11{:}10\) am, the remaining two thirds take only another \(160\) minutes, giving a completion time of \(1{:}50\) pm. Thus the displayed conditions alone do not determine a unique time. Under the intended constant-rate assumption, the answer is \(4{:}30\) pm, choice \(D\).
solutions.title: Equal thirds at a constant rate
